issues.acceptance: A representative native-renderer before/after capture reports raw frame times, one-percent low, hitch count, CPU/GPU attribution, and named script hot paths with 3, 5, 10, and 18 active enemies. Enemy separation is computed once from a cached stable roster per physics cycle, QA instrumentation performs no per-frame deep state snapshot or scene-wide scan in ordinary play, and AI behavior/spacing remains unchanged. llvmpipe evidence is recorded only as collector evidence.
issues.actual: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.
issues.expected: Ordinary gameplay performs bounded enemy steering and lightweight production work per frame; deep QA snapshots run only on demand or at a bounded debug sampling cadence.
issues.next_action: Capture native-renderer CPU/GPU profiler evidence, remove duplicate peer scans and sorts, and gate or sample QA-only deep observation.

blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `clean_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Restore the accepted enemy rifle presentation first, then make the complete native product shell criterion-ready while carrying fullscreen clarity through verification-first isolation and preserving clean boot, ordinary controls, encounter fixtures, and terminal result paths.

diagnosis.root_cause: The forced animation regression is product-wrapper drift from the last user-accepted rifle adapter: later per-frame pose, contact, and stock-height compensation replaced a stable direct binding. The fullscreen issue is now an evidence-boundary problem unless a fresh source audit disproves the candidate's unified settings transaction: its latest candidate detector is inactive, while representative native-renderer confirmation remains outstanding. The broader shell criterion still requires responsive, state-bound page behavior across the complete application flow.

stop_conditions: Stop animation work if it would require replacing, extracting, or surgically modifying the preserved humanoid package, imported meshes, skeleton, AnimationLibrary, skins, rifle asset, collision, or world scale.

If the display audit proves that the candidate already has one correct persisted display transaction and only representative native-renderer evidence is missing, make no speculative display edit and hand the issue to Tester as insufficient evidence pending native recapture.

Stop and repair before handoff if clean boot, physical G deployment, captured mouse look, pause/resume, encounter prepare/advance stability, checkpoint recovery, or success/failure result entry regresses.
Do not create tasks or target paths for the backlog enemy-AI, combat-feedback, audio/VFX/lighting, performance, review, weapon-report audio, or hot-path-stutter surfaces.

strategy.rationale: Use two materially different treatments instead of repeating prior tuning: atomically restore the last accepted enemy presentation wrapper and remove the compensating overlay stack; then isolate candidate-owned shell/display behavior from native-renderer evidence, changing display code only when the source and settled receipt show a real mismatch. The second task also completes the selected shell criterion as a player-facing flow rather than reducing it to one resolution measurement.

code: Developer parses and loads every changed script and scene, then runs the frozen clean-boot validation with no new candidate errors.
Inspect the enemy wrapper for the accepted position, rotation, roll, and scale tuple and for removal of the rejected procedural compensation calls; verify no imported component source was modified.
Inspect display ownership for one persisted transaction and verify its state receipt contains requested and settled physical-window, viewport, content-scale, and render-scale values.
Confirm all existing tester actions remain unbound, debug-only, release-guarded, and separated into stable preparation and explicit advancement semantics.
runtime: Developer self-validates from a fresh title boot using ordinary deployment, movement, mouse look, pause/resume, one ordinary enemy-contact smoke, checkpoint recovery, success/failure fixture entry, Replay, and available display transitions.

Tester recaptures the failed animation cells first in one loaded process, using the existing stable prepare and separate advance actions after an ordinary input smoke. Correlate skin, alive state, velocity, clip time, socket binding, rifle contact, and lifecycle generation before and after checkpoint recovery.

Tester performs a non-blocking adjacent patrol confirming that encounter-all prepare and first advance remain accepted and that no new occupancy, ballistic, input, runtime-error, or rendered-HUD regression was introduced; this patrol does not create or target backlog work.

Tester navigates title, briefing/loading, loadout, gameplay, pause/settings, ordinary death recovery, success result, failure result, and Replay with keyboard/mouse and gamepad, including settings persistence across restart and 200% UI scale behavior authority integration tests. e2e tests verify complete flow consistency and persistence; shell tests isolate navigation and resolution handling; no-?
visual: Capture matched representative-gameplay frames for both soldier skins in idle or aim, walk/run, fire, reload, the 60-second delayed branch, and checkpoint recovery. Add only the front, side, three-quarter, or contact close-up views needed to resolve rifle attachment, shoulder/hand contact, muzzle direction, posture, and foot grounding.

Capture full-viewport title/settings plus representative loading/briefing, loadout, pause, death-recovery, success, and failure states at 1280×720 100% and 1280×720 200%. Verify safe-area containment, readable hierarchy, focus treatment, grounded typography, and absence of clipping or opaque blockout presentation.

When representative native display is available, capture matched 1280×720 windowed and 1920×1080 fullscreen states and pair each frame with settled window, viewport, content-scale, and render-scale data. If native collection is unavailable, retain insufficient evidence without requesting speculative candidate edits.

done_when: The product-owned enemy presentation wrapper restores source position `(0, -4.8, 5)`, socket position `(0.02, 0.02, -0.02)`, socket rotation `(-90, 90, 0)`, the authored PI roll, and the accepted component scale.
Later per-frame aim, action, contact, stock-height, socket-pose, and hand-placement compensation no longer alters the restored baseline.

Both retained soldier skins show a continuously attached rifle with stable right-hand grip, support-hand contact, credible stock-to-shoulder placement, muzzle-forward alignment, upright hips and waist, and grounded feet through idle, aim, fire, reload, walk, and run.

A fresh deployment may remain idle with the current objective unsecured for at least 60 seconds and then resume toward B/C without a living actor becoming unarmed, pistol-like, prone, death/hit-terminal, detached, persistently hunched, foot-sliding, or a transform-only substitute.
